events.title: tvOS 27.2.1 and HomeView 27.2 Fix Bluetooth Pairing and Brotli Flaws
events.summary: A tvOS 27.2.1 update and HomeView Software 27.2 have been released to fix Bluetooth pairing bypass issues and a Brotli flaw that CISA lists as exploited. Related advisories cover a high-severity buffer overflow in a PLANET switch and an actively exploited XXE vulnerability in Cisco BroadWorks.
events.why_it_matters: The Brotli flaw, CVE-2026-111497, carries a CVSS of 9.2, is on CISA's KEV catalogue, and has an EPSS score of about 0.83, indicating significant exploitation risk. The Cisco BroadWorks XXE issue, CVE-2026-20320, is also KEV-listed and actively exploited. Defenders running the affected products should prioritise patching these items.

claims.text: CISA lists CVE-2026-111497 and CVE-2026-20320 as exploited in the wild.
CVE-2026-109445 is rated 9.3 (critical) under CVSS 4.0 by the CNA that assigned it, the highest of the 3 scored CVEs here.
FIRST's EPSS puts the chance of CVE-2026-111497 being exploited in the next 30 days at 82%, the highest of the 3 CVEs here.
A fix for brotli (PyPI) is published in 1.2.1, per GHSA-9v8h-qqgm-4m35.
A fix for brotlicffi (PyPI) is published in 1.2.1.0, per GHSA-9v8h-qqgm-4m35.

events.title: The Share Link Was Never the Lock: 35,578 Apps Wide Open
events.summary: Clarotec researchers tested 43,551 publicly published app addresses from xAI's Grok Build platform using a browser with no logged-in account and found 35,578 apps (94.7%) served their data without any authentication, with only 1,993 returning an authorization error.
events.why_it_matters: The record documents a systemic failure in a widely used AI app-building platform where publicly shared links bypass authentication checks, exposing anyone's deployed app data to unauthenticated strangers. Organizations that have built or deployed apps on agent platforms using share-link features should assume their apps may be similarly accessible and verify that server-side permission checks actually execute. Any platform shipping share features without authorization enforcement may share the same exposure pattern.

events.title: Data Breach at La Poste Subsidiary Maileva Affects 22 Million People in France
events.summary: A September cyberattack on Maileva, a subsidiary of France's La Poste group, exposed the names and postal addresses of about 22 million people in France, including patients and tenants, in what is described as one of the largest breaches the country has experienced. La Poste confirmed the incident.
events.why_it_matters: The scale — roughly 22 million people affected — makes this one of the largest breaches in France, and the stolen details (names and postal addresses) are well suited to targeted phishing and fraud campaigns. Organisations handling data via third-party mail and document services may face similar exposure through their vendors.
